md-gov-2026-cox-dan.name: Dan Cox
md-gov-2026-cox-dan.bio: Attorney, small-business owner, and former town council member and Maryland state delegate.

positions.stance: Will reverse added fees and plans to reduce the corporate and income tax rate to 4.9%.
Will "immediately bring power plants back online" and pursue clean energy methods such as SMRs and LNGs while preserving farmland and a clean Bay.
Will "use emergency order to begin the build for the Key Bridge immediately."
Will restore funding removed from the DDA budget and ensure the DDA community has a place at the table.
Will prioritize fully funded schools, resources for teachers, and "every dollar is going straight to the classrooms."

wi-gov-2026-crowley-david.name: David Crowley
wi-gov-2026-crowley-david.bio: Milwaukee County Executive in his second term; former state representative.

positions.stance: Will "grow an economy rooted in local ownership and union labor" and take his Building Bridges Program statewide.
Will modernize and expand apprenticeship and technical training programs connecting young people and career-changers to the trades, health care, and green energy.
Will streamline permitting, cut red tape for local entrepreneurs, and expand access to affordable capital.
"Government should help create jobs—not just write checks"; public investments in housing, health care, and climate resilience will come with clear expectations.
Will expand mobile outreach, addiction treatment access, and EMS innovations across the state.

co-gov-2026-marx-victor.name: Victor Marx
co-gov-2026-marx-victor.bio: Marine Corps veteran and founder of All Things Possible Ministries.

positions.stance: Will support legislation requiring Voter ID for all forms of voting, with a free state-issued voter identification card.
Will direct the Secretary of State to conduct mandatory annual voter list maintenance using cross-state data, death records, and change-of-address filings.
Will implement standardized chain-of-custody rules for ballots, equipment, and drop boxes, with logged documentation and bipartisan transport teams.
Will require bipartisan participation in ballot processing, signature verification, adjudication, tabulation, and post-election audits.
Will expand veterans' access to long-term care, memory care, mental health treatment, and VA-partnered medical facilities.

co-gov-2026-weiser-phil.name: Phil Weiser
co-gov-2026-weiser-phil.bio: Colorado Attorney General; former law clerk to U.S. Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg.

positions.stance: Will boost homes Coloradans can afford, "increasing attainable owner-occupied homes by 40,000."
Will preserve funding for prenatal and early childhood programs and launch a Childcare Solutions Fund to invest in local childcare solutions.
Will support teachers with livable wages, "stand strong for public schools," lower college costs, and expand Universal Preschool.
Will promote "a just transition," retraining workers for clean energy jobs including geothermal drilling.
Will establish "Primary Care for All," moving from a "sick care" system to a value-based "health care" system focused on prevention.

mn-gov-2026-klobuchar-amy.name: Amy Klobuchar
mn-gov-2026-klobuchar-amy.bio: U.S. Senator and former Hennepin County Attorney.

positions.stance: Will work to lower costs for health care, housing, child care, and utility bills, including lowering prescription drug prices and building more homes.
Intends to make state government "innovative, effective, and accountable," starting by rooting out fraud.
Will double apprenticeships and workforce training and raise academic achievement with a focus on reading and math.
Will take on organized crime and gang violence and help local police departments hire and retain more officers.
Will expand Minnesota's rural economy by helping businesses and farmers grow products, find new markets, and export, and by supporting rural hospitals and broadband.

mn-gov-2026-demuth-lisa.name: Lisa Demuth
mn-gov-2026-demuth-lisa.bio: Minnesota House Republican leader and state representative since 2018; former small-business owner and ROCORI School Board member.

positions.stance: Will cut income taxes by reducing the lowest two brackets, dial back car tab fees, and end taxes on Social Security benefits.
Will "end the culture of fraud and corruption in state government" and work to pass a non-partisan Office of Inspector General.
Will invest in public safety resources for cities and counties and strengthen sentences for repeat offenders.
Will "repeal Minnesota's longstanding ban on nuclear energy" and reform mandates she says are driving up heating and electric bills.
Will "lead an education revolution that puts academic excellence and reading proficiency at the center of our agenda."

sc-gov-2026-wilson-alan.name: Alan Wilson
sc-gov-2026-wilson-alan.bio: South Carolina Attorney General, first elected in 2010, and Army National Guard combat veteran.

positions.stance: Will work with law enforcement to dismantle criminal networks and strengthen penalties for fentanyl and violent offenders.
Will fully fund public schools, expand school choice, and focus on early childhood literacy and technical and vocational education.
Will make roads, bridges, and infrastructure a priority to prepare for economic development and population growth.
Will support rural clinics, expand telemedicine, and incentivize medical professionals to serve under-served areas.
Is "firmly pro-life" and "will always support laws that defend the unborn."

sc-gov-2026-johnson-jermaine.name: Jermaine Johnson
sc-gov-2026-johnson-jermaine.bio: South Carolina state representative since 2020, nonprofit founder, consultant, and adjunct professor.

positions.stance: Plans to increase the share of families who do not pay income tax to 70%.
Will work with municipalities to reduce property taxes for working families.
Will fund a grant program allowing municipalities to convert existing structures into affordable housing units.
Will create a labor advisory council to recommend a state minimum wage, remove employment barriers, and fight wage theft.
Wrote a bill letting municipalities fix their own roads and bridges with money from the state Department of Transportation.
Will "declare a one year moratorium on data centers" and offer no tax breaks or nondisclosure agreements for data center companies.
Would suspend the gas tax when prices spike, eliminate the grocery tax, raise wages including the minimum wage, and end taxes on overtime.
Would create a state Earned Income Tax Credit, expand childcare, offer free community college for adults without credentials, and strengthen apprenticeship incentives.
Would expand Medicaid to cover more than 154,000 working Alabamians and strengthen rural healthcare.
Would ban elected officials from trading individual stocks, promote citizen-led ballot initiatives, and expand early voting.

al-gov-2026-tuberville-tommy.name: Tommy Tuberville
al-gov-2026-tuberville-tommy.bio: U.S. Senator from Alabama since 2021 and former college football coach.

positions.stance: Opposes men competing in women's sports and says CRT and DEI "should have no place in our government or our schools."
Will "further reduce taxes, get rid of waste, and make life in Alabama more affordable" and work to bring back manufacturing.
Will "back the blue, enforce the law, and work with President Trump to deport illegal alien criminals."
Will expand school choice so "parents, not the government, are in charge of their child's educational future."
Believes in the right to bear arms; to those who want to take guns: "come and take it."

al-ltgov-2026-ensler-phillip.name: Phillip Ensler
al-ltgov-2026-ensler-phillip.bio: Civil rights lawyer, former teacher, and Alabama House representative.

positions.stance: Will continue to fight to give Alabamians the right to vote on a lottery, with revenue usable for rebate checks and education.
Will resist attacks on Medicaid and Medicare and supports expanding Medicaid to cover all Alabamians who don't qualify for ACA subsidies.
Supports pegging teachers' salaries to the cost of living and increasing retiree benefits.
Supports safe-storage requirements for firearms and a red flag law.
Supports banning nondisclosure agreements with data centers and a moratorium on new data center construction until a rigorous review process exists.

al-ltgov-2026-wahl-john.name: John Wahl
al-ltgov-2026-wahl-john.bio: Former chairman of the Alabama Republican Party and farmer.

positions.stance: Believes the Constitution protects "God-given rights" and will defend freedom of speech and religion against government overreach.
Supports pro-growth policies that reduce red tape, plus job training, workforce development, and energy independence.
Supports "meaningful tax relief" and cutting wasteful government spending.
Supports President Trump's plan to secure the southern border, finish the wall, and stop illegal immigration.
Will work to ensure "every legal vote is counted accurately" and that elections are secure and transparent.
Will expand infant and toddler childcare access while creating a pathway to universal preschool statewide.
Will expand options for renters and first-time buyers, cut red tape for new construction, and increase starter homes and down payment assistance.
Will strengthen mental health and addiction care access, fight insurance rate hikes, and defend the Oregon Health Plan from Medicaid cuts.
Will ban personal-data-based pricing schemes, crack down on hidden fees, and stop the use of AI to deny insurance claims.
Will defend against tariffs, cuts to SNAP, and "any federal policies that raise costs for Oregonians."

or-gov-2026-drazan-christine.name: Christine Drazan
or-gov-2026-drazan-christine.bio: Former Oregon House Republican Leader and former chief of staff to the Oregon House Speaker.

positions.stance: Will issue a Day One Affordability Executive Order, veto new tax and fee increases, and repeal the Climate Protection Program executive order.
Will declare Oregon "Open for Business," freeze new regulations, and create a $200 million site readiness and infrastructure fund.
Will fully audit homeless services and addiction spending and prioritize addiction recovery and mental health treatment.
Seeks a 120-day maximum decision period for qualifying housing projects and expanded first-time homebuyer programs.
Will reinstate meaningful graduation requirements and end social promotion by ensuring students read proficiently by third grade.

ok-gov-2026-mazzei-mike.name: Mike Mazzei
ok-gov-2026-mazzei-mike.bio: Former Oklahoma state senator and business leader.

positions.stance: Plans to eliminate property tax for seniors and veterans "to protect homeownership and lower the cost of living."
Will safeguard "farmland, energy assets, and property rights from foreign control."
"Reforming education so kids can read, graduate, and succeed in the real world."
"Creating an environment where businesses grow and workers earn more."
"Restoring discipline, transparency, and trust in state government."

ok-gov-2026-munson-cyndi.name: Cyndi Munson
ok-gov-2026-munson-cyndi.bio: Oklahoma state representative since 2015 and former House Minority Leader; previously worked in the nonprofit sector.

positions.stance: Will work to institute mandatory paid family leave for parental and family caregiving.
Will fully fund public schools, raise teacher and support staff pay, and repeal the Parental Choice Tax voucher program.
Will oppose Medicaid cuts and expand prenatal, maternity, and mental health care access, especially in rural Oklahoma.
Will issue a day-one moratorium on new data center construction and end giveaways to large out-of-state corporations.
Wants to increase the childcare tax credit, sales tax relief credit, and Earned Income Tax Credit; opposes further income tax cuts for the wealthiest.

ok-ltgov-2026-shannon-tw.name: T. W. Shannon
ok-ltgov-2026-shannon-tw.bio: Former Speaker of the Oklahoma House, Oklahoma Transportation Commissioner, community bank CEO, and senior advisor in President Trump's administration.

positions.stance: Lists "Grow our economy" as a campaign priority.
Lists "Cut taxes & red tape" as a campaign priority.
Lists "Support farmers & ranchers" as a campaign priority.
Lists "Back law enforcement" as a campaign priority.
Lists "Defend our freedoms" as a campaign priority.

ok-ltgov-2026-forbes-kelly.name: Kelly Forbes
ok-ltgov-2026-forbes-kelly.bio: Educator who has served as a classroom teacher, school administrator, federal programs director, and adjunct professor.

positions.stance: Will invest in small businesses, strengthen Career-Tech, work with Native Nations, and expand workforce training.
Will build "a strong, well-funded public education system" that "keeps public dollars in public schools."
Will expand access, incentivize healthcare professionals in underserved areas, and ensure culturally responsive care.
Will promote Oklahoma tourism around the Route 66 centennial and 2028 Olympic events.
Committed to transparent, accountable government and "restoring trust in our state government."

ct-gov-2026-lamont-ned.name: Ned Lamont
ct-gov-2026-lamont-ned.bio: Governor of Connecticut and former business owner.

positions.stance: Supports universal pre-K, universal free school meals, expanded healthcare access, more housing supply, and stronger paid family leave.
Would require affordability to be considered in utility profits and hold utilities accountable through stronger oversight.
Would require large corporations with employees on HUSKY (Medicaid) to contribute up to $1,000 per employee to lower premiums.
Committed to finishing universal pre-K with sustainable long-term funding while supporting childcare workers and providers.
Will increase state support for special education and support teachers and school staff.

ct-gov-2026-fazio-ryan.name: Ryan Fazio
ct-gov-2026-fazio-ryan.bio: Connecticut state senator who has worked in energy, agriculture, and shipping.

positions.stance: Would reduce state income-tax rates, "providing more than $2.5 billion in annual tax relief when fully implemented."
Plans to cut electricity bills by 20% "by ending hidden taxes, expanding reliable supply, and removing the mandates driving up costs."
Would lower income taxes for every family by $1,500 and implement property tax caps.
Supports reducing housing costs, growing supply, and protecting local control of zoning and decision-making.
Will end the 20-year property and sales tax break for data centers.
Will protect life before birth, end state benefits for illegal immigrants, defend Second Amendment rights, and lower the tax burden.
Supports independent state-level safety testing of agricultural products and reducing agrichemical runoff.
Will fund the IWiLL program, enhance water monitoring, and create conservation incentives "to prevent contamination at the source."
Supports reducing property taxes, banning Wall Street hedge funds from buying single-family homes, and raising taxes on data centers.
Supports ending illegal foreign ownership of farmland, protecting right to repair, and "ending eminent domain for private corporate gain."
Will work to restore the State Auditor's ability to find misspent tax dollars.
Will "reverse the privatization of Medicaid the same way it was passed – by an executive order."
Pledged a program letting state employees who can work anywhere live anywhere in Iowa, to help revitalize small towns.
Supports universal all-day pre-K, paid for by ending voucher spending on wealthy families, and more oversight of vouchers.
Supports a public top-four primary open to all eligible voters and Approval Voting in the general election.

nv-gov-2026-ford-aaron.name: Aaron D. Ford
nv-gov-2026-ford-aaron.bio: Nevada Attorney General and former public school math teacher.

positions.stance: Will stand up to tariffs, crack down on Wall Street firms buying homes, and ease permitting to encourage new construction.
Will address predatory practices by Pharmacy Benefit Managers and implement a medical debt relief program.
Will prioritize clean and affordable energy and stand up to utility demand charges.
Will stop data center tax breaks until they prove results and require data centers to bring their own clean energy, grid infrastructure, and water.

nv-gov-2026-lombardo-joseph.name: Joseph Lombardo
nv-gov-2026-lombardo-joseph.bio: Governor of Nevada, former sheriff, and U.S. Army and Nevada National Guard veteran.

positions.stance: Will target healthcare as an industry and train more doctors, nurses, and health professionals in Nevada with incentives to stay.
Will expand down payment support under the Attainable Housing Program and cut red tape to build homes faster.
"Every child reads at grade level by third grade"; will raise per-pupil funding along with accountability and support school options.
Will "maintain commitment to No New Taxes" and champion an annual back-to-school sales tax holiday.
Will close the fentanyl trafficking threshold loophole and ensure violent and repeat offenders serve their sentences.

nv-ltgov-2026-anthony-stavros.name: Stavros Anthony
nv-ltgov-2026-anthony-stavros.bio: Nevada's Lieutenant Governor, retired Las Vegas Metro police captain, and former Las Vegas City Council member.

positions.stance: Strongly supports Governor Lombardo's law-and-order efforts and ensuring law enforcement agencies "have the resources they need."
Will "continue to fight in every way possible to ensure our female athletes in Nevada are treated with fairness."

nv-ltgov-2026-jauregui-sandra.name: Sandra Jauregui
nv-ltgov-2026-jauregui-sandra.bio: Nevada state legislator and Assembly Majority Leader with prior work in housing relief programs.

positions.stance: Will fight tariffs she calls illegal and protect "the right to access abortion and birth control."
Believes "healthcare is a fundamental right" and will fight to lower prescription drug costs.
Will take on private equity companies and hedge funds buying housing and protect renters' and homeowners' rights.
Will continue "to keep guns out of the hands of dangerous criminals, domestic abusers, and terrorists."
Will expand partnerships with unions, community colleges, and businesses to create paid apprenticeships and job training programs.
Will create regional economic hubs and rebuild roads, water, sewer, and broadband infrastructure.
Will invest in literacy, strengthen early education, expand school mental health support, and support teachers with fair pay.
Will stop construction of the Franklin County prison and focus on rehabilitation, workforce training, and reentry programs.
Will protect Medicaid, expand maternal and mental health services, and use telehealth to reach rural communities.

ar-ltgov-2026-rutledge-leslie.name: Leslie Rutledge
ar-ltgov-2026-rutledge-leslie.bio: Lieutenant Governor of Arkansas since 2023 and former two-term Arkansas Attorney General.

positions.stance: Will "fight to secure my fellow Americans' rights to bear arms just as vigorously as I protect Arkansans."
Will "ensure our pro-life and pro-family values remain protected from assaults from the far-left."
Believes "our state's rights should remain protected from illegal Federal action."
Says "we must ensure our brave have a place to call home."
Says she has taken opioid manufacturers to court, introduced prevention education programs, and worked with law enforcement to collect unused opioids.
